title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault‑Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) executed under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution used the declared model version gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (<= planned maximum 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces were recorded during execution and enable deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, expand on experimental design rationale and paired estimand semantics, analyze the observed discordant-pair structure and representative failure modes from validator traces, and state limitations and reproducibility guidance without altering the preregistered scientific record.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): produce candidate configurations, check them with deterministic verifiers, and feed verifier diagnostics back to a generator/repair model when violations are found. Prior controlled and benchmarked work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code shows that deterministic verifiers interposed between probabilistic generation and acceptance raise verifier-detected pass rates but expose new failure modes and incur interaction costs [1]–[4]. Field and survey studies caution that read-oriented assistance does not automatically imply safe closed-loop automated changes in network operations [5].

Research question and contribution. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor command-line interface (CLI) templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. We ask: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults? To answer this, we executed a preregistered paired experiment that deterministically injected actionable faults, reused the same controlled-fault candidate across both arms (shared_controlled_fault_candidate), and compared blind repair (baseline) versus verifier-guided repair (guarded) under a matched repair-budget contract. Our main contribution is the preregistered confirmatory estimate of the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) and a detailed evidence-grounded interpretation of the observed discordant-pair structure and failure modes using archived per-episode validator traces.
sections.related_work:
Empirical evaluations of GVR-like architectures in code, IaC, and DSL tasks show consistent gains in verifier pass rates when repair is guided by deterministic diagnostics or tests; however, scope and tradeoffs vary by domain and verifier design [1,2]. Analyses of verifier-mediated iterative refinement document two recurring caveats: (a) optimization toward a single verifier proxy can cause verifier-exploitation, where artifacts satisfy the verifier but degrade unmeasured target properties [3]; and (b) verifier-mediated workflows impose a measurable interaction and compute overhead (a "verifier tax") whose magnitude depends on horizon and design choices [4]. Surveys and field case studies in NetOps indicate helpfulness for read/write support but emphasize weaker guarantees as systems become more agentic and closed-loop, motivating controlled fault-injection evaluations specific to vendor CLI templates [5].

How this study differs. Most prior controlled demonstrations concentrate on IaC or DSLs where verifiers and the mapping from artifacts to verifier signals are tightly matched. Our experiment addresses a gap identified in the literature: a preregistered, deterministic fault-injection paired study applied to vendor-CLI templates with archived validator traces that permit inspection of specific failure classes, difficulty strata, and harmful-change indicators (see Evidence Synthesis and preregistration). We do not claim generalization beyond the synthetic controlled-fault bank, nor do we claim operational readiness; instead, we provide controlled, artifact-backed evidence about the isolated effect of exposing deterministic diagnostic feedback to an LLM repair model under matched source generation and repair budgets.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a binary success requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance check to accept the post-repair candidate.

Adapter and pairing semantics. Confirmatory execution used the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. Under that contract each task index received exactly one deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate which was reused unchanged across both experimental conditions; exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms. Both arms therefore received the same initial candidate and matched repair-call budgets. Baseline denotes blind repair (repair without exposure of verifier diagnostics) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed to the repair model. Because source generation and controlled-fault assignment are shared, observed between-condition differences isolate the effect of diagnostics exposure under matched generation and repair resources.

Model sampling and runtime parameters. The declared model used was gpt-5-mini. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Execution performed exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair that was reused by both conditions under the adapter contract; the design does not measure effects of independent first-pass sampling across conditions.

Controlled-challenge fault bank and scoring rules. The confirmatory bank comprised 40 preregistered deterministic fault indices constructed from vendor-CLI templates; faults were injected to guarantee activation of validator diagnostics (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). The primary success predicate required agreement of the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance check. A frozen harmful-change labeling mapping (labeling PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE and UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE as harmful) was preregistered; that mapping and the per-episode validator traces were recorded during execution and permit deterministic recomputation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic by independent auditors.

Statistical plan and missingness. The predefined primary test was a two-sided exact paired binary test (exact McNemar or equivalent). We report discordant-pair counts (n10, n01), the absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Missingness handling followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule: exclude a pair only if both executions are unscorable; one pair was excluded because its source generation was unscorable per the preregistered rule.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed pairs = 39 (one pair excluded because its shared source generation was unscorable). Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9, n01 = 1, n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507. Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729).

Discordant-pair structure and representative evidence. The discordant pattern (n10 = 9 >> n01 = 1) indicates that most gains derive from guarded episodes that corrected verifier-detectable violations left unresolved by blind repair. Per-episode validator traces archived with the execution show repeated diagnostic patterns: (a) medium-difficulty faults such as 'shutdown_configure_restore' where blind repairs sometimes omitted the final restore step (example pair task-000001; guarded restored the required command sequence and baseline occasionally left FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH), and (b) hard protected-interface faults (e.g., 'protected_interface_change') where guarded repairs used explicit PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE diagnostics to avoid touching protected fields. Representative artifact entries (validator_trace.violation_codes, injected_validation.difficulty.level, and validation_after.valid flags) support these mechanistic observations without introducing new measurements.

Missingness and unresolved preregistered safety aggregation. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation was not computed in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference. The frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validator traces required to compute that preregistered statistic were recorded during execution and permit deterministic independent recomputation; any harmful-overrepair numbers computed outside the archived confirmatory summary are exploratory.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and mechanism. Under shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing, both arms received the identical faulty candidate and matched repair budgets; the observed improvement therefore isolates the effect of exposing deterministic validator diagnostics to the repair model. The majority of discordant outcomes were guarded-only successes (n10 = 9), consistent with diagnostics enabling targeted corrective edits (e.g., reinserting an omitted restore command or avoiding protected-interface edits). Representative validator traces (difficulty levels, violation_codes lists, and normalized_configuration diffs) document these repair patterns at the episode level.

Statistical uncertainty, ceiling effects, and power. The observed absolute paired difference is +20.51 percentage points with p = 0.0215 and a 95% paired-bootstrap CI that excludes zero. The baseline success rate (≈77%) is moderately high, leaving a limited room-to-improve ceiling; the guarded condition approaches a practical ceiling in this controlled bank (≈97%). The preregistered power plan targeted larger effects (~30 percentage points) with n = 40; the observed discordant counts provided sufficient power to detect the realized 20.5 percentage-point effect in this confirmatory run but limit precision for finer-grained subgroup inferences.

Failure modes, safety boundary, and unresolved safety verdict. The archived validator traces reveal two salient failure-mode clusters: (1) omission class — repairs that omitted required commands (e.g., missing restore) leading to FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH, and (2) harmful-change class — repairs that touched protected interfaces or induced UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. Guarded repairs reduced omission-class residuals by leveraging explicit violation codes. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory safety aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary, so we do not assert a confirmatory safety verdict here. The recorded frozen mapping and per-episode traces enable deterministic recomputation of that safety statistic by independent auditors, and any such recomputation should be treated as exploratory unless surfaced in a confirmatory artifact.

Operational implications and verifier tax. Exposing diagnostics materially improved verifier+simulator-validated success for the tested controlled fault bank; however, verifier-guided workflows increase model–verifier interactions: confirmatory execution used 118 hosted-model calls under the matched budget constraint. Assessing operational feasibility (the verifier tax tradeoffs) requires broader deployment-scale studies that measure latency, cost per avoided failure, and human-in-the-loop triage overheads. Our execution accounting and reconciliation artifacts provide the instrumentation needed for such exploratory cost calculations.

Mitigations and broader risks. Prior work shows verifier-exploitation risk when single-proxy verifiers are optimized iteratively [3]. Our short-horizon, single-repair opportunity and shared-candidate design reduce but do not eliminate exploitation risk in longer agentic chains. Practical mitigations include multi-verifier ensembles, explicit harmful-change constraints (the frozen harmful-change mapping is an example), calibrated abstention, and uncertainty quantification. These measures merit systematic evaluation in future replications across models and verifiers.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is constrained by model sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null/unset) and exactly-one initial sampled generation per pair; differences across arms reflect diagnostics exposure under the adapter contract rather than independent first-pass generation. Construct validity is limited by requiring agreement between a deterministic verifier and a simulator; both components shape what we measure as “valid.” External validity is limited by (a) a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and (b) a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank; generalization to diverse vendor equipment and naturalistic operator streams is untested. Conclusion validity: the confirmatory sample (complete_pairs = 39) yields a statistically detectable effect of the observed magnitude but restricts power for per-fault-class inference.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using a hosted validator-feedback repair adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). The result is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic verifier and simulator used in execution. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces recorded during execution provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction of that statistic. We recommend replication across multiple models and multi-verifier ensembles, explicit confirmatory computation of harmful-overrepair aggregations, and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Exact initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation mappings needed to reproduce the preregistered secondary aggregations were recorded in the archived evidence bundle. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
